subject: Computer Networking
title: VPNs: Tunnels Through the Internet
description: A fast breakdown of VPNs: Tunnels Through the Internet for builders.

hook.text: You're on airport Wi-Fi. Anyone nearby could snoop on your traffic. A VPN wraps it in an encrypted tunnel.

buildup.text: A VPN routes your traffic through a remote server. Websites see the VPN's IP address, not yours.

discovery.text: This hides your browsing from your ISP and local network. It also lets you appear to be in another country.

twist.text: But the VPN provider can see your traffic instead. You're just shifting trust, not eliminating it.

climax.text: Companies use VPNs to let remote workers access internal systems securely, as if they were in the office.

punchline.text: A VPN hides your traffic. It doesn't make you invisible.

quiz.question: What does a VPN actually do to your internet traffic?
options: Encrypts it and routes it through a remote server
Makes your connection faster by compressing data

details.summary: Virtual Private Networks create encrypted tunnels through the public internet, making your traffic appear to come from the VPN server's location. VPNs protect privacy on untrusted networks, bypass geographic restrictions, and connect remote offices securely.
details.whyItMatters: VPNs are widely used for privacy and security. Understanding how they work helps evaluate when they actually protect you and when they do not.
takeaways: VPNs create encrypted tunnels through the public internet
Your traffic appears to originate from the VPN server location
VPNs protect on untrusted networks but do not provide anonymity

faq.question: Does a VPN make you anonymous?
faq.answer: No. A VPN hides your activity from your ISP and local network, but the VPN provider can see all your traffic. Websites can still identify you through cookies, browser fingerprinting, and login credentials. A VPN shifts trust from your ISP to the VPN provider.

faq.question: When should you use a VPN?
faq.answer: Use a VPN on public Wi-Fi to prevent eavesdropping. Use it to access your company's internal network remotely. Use it to bypass geographic content restrictions. Do not rely on a VPN for true anonymity or to hide illegal activity. Choose a provider with a verified no-logs policy.
